subject: menu shell
defect: The full-screen charcoal menu with thin teal borders has little visual hierarchy or scenic connection to the illustrated world
notes: Same full-screen shell in Meadows and Tidewake production UI; assess Cloudreach and Stormwood before final shared exposure.

subject: map
defect: The map canvas shows headings and markers without visible terrain or road context for the displayed destinations
notes: First Shore is marked discovered but the Day 1 state may hide survey detail; both biome maps lack terrain/route context at this state.

subject: Team Tether stronghold
defect: The stronghold reads as a small dark ruin behind dominant pylons on approach and as a broad sparsely dressed stone room up close
notes: The generic capture stands are not verified route approaches; reshoot the authored approach before work is assigned.

subject: exploration HUD
defect: The many dark boxed HUD panels and outlined text occupy a large share of the exploration view
notes: Tidewake exterior confirms the large team strip quest box quick bar and shortcut bar; Meadows frame is indoors. Cloudreach flight frames show the same panels crowding airborne scenery.

subject: ground cover
defect: Thin grass and the same tall white flowers repeat over broad green slopes with few clustered color or rock breaks
notes: Repeated across several Meadows regions; compare route-walk samples before expanding sightings.

subject: mill and settlements
defect: The mill water is a broad flat blue surface with abrupt sparse banks and nearby settlements have little concentrated visible activity
notes: This merges the recurring lack of lively scene composition; split if later captures show independent causes or owners.

subject: secondary menu panels
defect: The Quests Build and Players panels leave most of their area empty around a few plain text lines or a single button
notes: The Day 1 fixture may explain empty panels, but the screen leaves large dead areas. Skills capture still resembles Quests; verify navigation.

subject: shore landforms
defect: Repeated grassy domes with steep smooth gray rock skirts lack layered shore ecology and clear grass-to-sand transitions
notes: Confirmed across four seeded route/off-route frames; gray rock skirts and abrupt green tops are visible at near and far range.

subject: water and island depth
defect: Broad offshore water reads as uniform light cyan with little depth variation across several island routes
notes: Brine Steps shore has strong foam and wave detail; this row concerns open-water distance views only.

subject: Veilfall silhouette
defect: The distant Veilfall mountain reads as a near-geometric dark cone with narrow broken waterfall streaks
notes: The near cascade has a broad white curtain and mist in the route frame; limit this defect to far silhouette and landmark legibility.

subject: named destination read
defect: Several named route destinations read as unmarked grassy slopes or small generic structures instead of distinct halls arches or terraces
notes: Seeded route proxy corroborates generic location stands; reshoot true authored route before assigning site work. The Gull Rest tower itself remains a visible local marker.

subject: Burrow Warrens hillside
defect: The hillside beside the Burrow entrance exposes a broad rectangular brown terrain face with straight edges and a dark cut
notes: Repeated in two seeded off-route stands; check authored entrance approach for extent.

subject: Tether Relay yard
defect: Tall flowers and grass grow densely through the flat trafficked relay yard around guards crates and ramp
notes: Two ordinary camera views at the route proxy.

subject: distant mountains
defect: The mountain backdrop has hard isolated facets and dark slash shapes instead of continuous landform silhouettes
notes: Distant backdrop defect is separate from near-ground repetition; check if this backdrop is shared with another biome.

subject: creature collapse and rest
defect: Several fainted bodies remain upright or float above the grass and some resting poses do not settle onto the ground
notes: The direct pose fixture needs confirmation in a real faint/rest transition; explicit hovering is visible in Trailpup and Veridian. Cloudreach resting Cloudfang Solmane and Tempestwing show clear ground separation in stills; flying faint states may have different gameplay rules.

subject: creature hurt and movement poses
defect: Hurt and moving frames often retain the idle silhouette so the state is difficult to read without a filename
notes: Still frames cannot establish locomotion timing; check production transition captures before scheduling animation work. Tidewake and Stormwood stills confirm the recurring state-read gap; judge motion before assigning animation timing.

subject: normal creature scale
defect: Several normal creatures read visibly shorter than the trainer in the shared near-framed scale view
notes: Apparent visual height varies with perspective and posture; compare with declared size and a level camera before adjusting assets. Stormwood near-framed size comparison confirms this in five additional species. Cloudreach smaller species remain below trainer size in the common stage; exact authored scale versus perspective needs verification.

subject: shiny palette distinction
defect: Some shiny variants have no reliably readable colour-block difference from their normal form at the device view
notes: Other species have strong shiny distinctions; assess these pairs at the same lighting and camera.

subject: alpha rarity read
defect: Several alpha variants read mainly as a modest size increase without a distinct staged presence beside the trainer
notes: Mosshell alpha has a stronger looming silhouette; a staged world encounter may read differently from this controlled pair.

subject: creature ground contact
defect: Dense foreground grass obscures several creatures feet and lower outlines in the normal camera view
notes: Do not infer floating from grass occlusion alone; explicit hover is cataloged in P2-015.

subject: open terrain
defect: Broad level grass fields and sparse ordinary trees dominate Cloudreach views where layered elevated land and ledge detail should lead the route
notes: Code-blind location verdict. Some generic teleport stands may face away from authored elevated route; compare a route-grounded frame matrix before final assignment.

subject: summit aviary
defect: The summit landmark reads as a small skeletal dome on grass beside a separate court instead of a layered stone sanctuary and its night silhouette stays dark
notes: A recognizable distance marker exists but the hero structure is visually thin in approach and close views.

subject: exposed landform edges
defect: Floating island undersides form blunt dark slabs and several cliffs and grassy shelves have conspicuous straight extruded edges
notes: Grouped as one recurring exposed-edge geometry defect; inspect whether cliff and island meshes share an authoring path.

subject: architectural landmark read
defect: Several Cloudreach destinations present sparse plain or disconnected structures with weak landmark-specific detail
notes: Usable approach frames support this; close observatory captures are pressed against the wall and should be reshot. Flight Aerie route/vista also lacks a recognizable built silhouette; route sampling may face away, so verify with authored approach. Stormward close views show isolated short walls, flat banners, detached cobble insets and a suspended emblem; its authored stand is usable.

subject: grass and stone finish
defect: Tall grass intrudes through shrine paving while repeated grass and simple stone surfaces reduce close-range material distinction across sites
notes: The shrine close frame is partly wall-obstructed but grass intersection is visible; confirm on a corrected stand.

subject: Veilfall approach shallows
defect: A ruler-straight chain of nearly identical tan discs with white rims makes the Veilfall approach read as mechanical stepping stones rather than natural current shallows
notes: Recurring from three route views; the thin white water marks reinforce the straight disc chain.

subject: creature faint state
defect: Several fainted aquatic creatures keep raised alert heads or upright crouches instead of reading as defeated
notes: Mirejaw and Mangrove Monitor show stronger contrasting collapses; validate in a real encounter.

subject: creature rest poses
defect: Riptusk and Torrentoad resting poses roll onto their backs with limbs raised and read as distressed rather than settled
notes: Grass obscures contact edges; no floating conclusion from these frames.

subject: shiny creature finish
defect: Several shiny variants become near-uniform hot magenta and lose their ordinary species material and pattern identity
notes: Variants are easy to identify; Ripplet and Mosshell retain more form detail.

subject: settings and binding instructions
defect: Dense gray-on-navy control instructions and literal key labels make settings and quick binding text hard to scan
notes: Shared menu presentation in two biomes; [Minus] and [Equal] labels are visible in map instructions.

subject: map active region
defect: The current region map heading is shown while the Meadows region tab appears more active than the displayed biome tab
notes: Could be Day 1 fixture navigation state rather than product selection behavior; verify after explicitly selecting Tidewake. Stormwood repeats the apparent tab mismatch at zero survey; verify selection after navigating the region list.

subject: ground pickup identity
defect: Candies and potions read mainly as small colored glows in Meadows while unrelated Tidewake pickups repeat one crate and Cloudreach potion/revive pickups read as plants
notes: Twelve Tidewake named families use the same small crate with hue changes; representative sightings are listed. Cloudreach potion_large appears as a glowing red-budded plant and revive as a blue flower. Five Cloudreach item frames did not isolate their subject. Stormwood candy is visible; 19 other planned pickup frames need targeted reshoot.

subject: harvest reward identity
defect: Several reward harvest nodes read as generic crates or vegetation without a clear visible connection to their named item
notes: Stone and ironwood have stronger node silhouettes; check whether reward item is intentionally hidden until interaction.

subject: camp and workshop prop legibility
defect: Small camp and workshop props overlap nearby signs grass creatures or other tools so individual objects are difficult to pick out
notes: The CAMP sign and workshop camera stands contribute to occlusion; reshoot side views before assigning every prop as a scene issue.

subject: filled container distinction
defect: Apple crates and barrels look nearly the same as their empty or ordinary counterparts from the normal side view
notes: A top view may reveal the contents; verify before work is assigned.

subject: Stormheart finale
defect: The Stormheart finale reads as a dark cylindrical ring with a hole rather than a giant living tree with a branching crown and visible core
notes: Daytime frames support the silhouette defect; dynamo-core approach is obstructed and excluded.

subject: named destination identities
defect: Several named destinations read as similar grass and trees without a distinct subject in the captured close views
notes: Generic camera stands may miss authored subjects; confirm with targeted route approaches before assigning each landmark.

subject: forest ground and distance layers
defect: Uniform grass and flower carpet across broad flat land weakens the deep wet ancient forest silhouette and distance layers
notes: Representative views across three named regions; night rain alone does not establish reflective pools or layered roots in these frames.

subject: charged road surface
defect: Thick gold lightning stripes dominate long stretches of road as a repeated flat pattern
notes: Captured at both day and night; assess alongside moving traversal footage if available.

subject: Crown Arch
defect: The Crown Arch appears as a small square blue frame on an exposed square slab with grass clipping through it
notes: The generic approach is tree-obstructed; close shot supports slab and silhouette concerns.

subject: Surge phase presentation
defect: Calm Building and Fading weather stills remain difficult to distinguish while Break reads mainly through darker lighting and heavier rain
notes: Two unobstructed fixed stands support the still-frame distinction gap; Crown Arch stand is blocked and excluded. Capture timed lightning and motion before judging flash rhythm wind response or afterglow.

subject: Glass Field spike bases
defect: Blue glass spikes rise from a flat dark base with grass passing through it and a rigid white segment crossing the cluster
notes: Close seeded route frame supports this placement and intersection defect; wide route and dusk vista retain a useful cyan landmark.

subject: electric creature finish
defect: Fulgocobra and Stormraven lack clear charged material contrast at normal creature-view distance
notes: Cobra reads mostly mottled brown with no visible charged seam; raven mostly uniform cobalt. Other Stormwood species show stronger electric accents.

subject: candy pickup tiers
defect: Good Great and Rare Candy use nearly the same green wrapped form and scale at normal camera distance
notes: The Tidewake skill candy I and II labels are tiny. Skill candy III was not isolated in its frame and needs a reshoot.

subject: harvest resource identity
defect: Several harvest nodes look like ordinary stone mushrooms trees or foliage without a readable cue for their named Stormwood material
notes: Voltcap is a stronger glowing node; the pictured stormglass rocks lack a glass read.

subject: Static Snap technique pickup
defect: The Static Snap technique pickup reads as a generic blue centered capture orb rather than a technique item
notes: The item is visible at normal distance; verify whether the same orb is intentionally used for all technique pickups.

subject: Cloudreach map region label
defect: The discovered Cloudreach Gate / Lower Cliffs label is cut after LOWER without a wrap or ellipsis
notes: The exploration HUD spells the full location at the same initial state; the map strip truncates it.

subject: floating dark strips
defect: Disconnected black rail-like strips cross grass and extend into open air above the Cloudreach void
notes: Clearly visible in the Stormward route frame; a second distant sighting may be the same prop family. Confirm from an authored stand.

subject: human post poses
defect: Many named villagers and trainers hold the same straight neutral stance with arms down despite different roles
notes: Post stills show neutral stances; dialogue and combat states have not been captured and may add variation.

subject: Mira shop counter
defect: Mira stands behind a large featureless tan rectangular counter that reads unfinished beside the detailed cottage
notes: Normal camera inside the shop with Mira visible at her authored post.

subject: Garrick post
defect: A brown head-like form at Garrick’s authored post appears to intersect two large rocks
notes: The character identity is uncertain in this frame; reshoot from a side stand before assigning a placement defect.

subject: Three Bells bridge marker
defect: A saturated cyan T-shaped post and glowing ring sit directly before the Three Bells Bridge and compete with the bells in the close view
notes: The wooden bridge and three bells read clearly; the central cyan marker lacks an apparent material or wayfinding role in the stills.

subject: mushroom pickup variants
defect: Speed Mushroom and Wild Mushroom use the same pale yellow mushroom cluster silhouette at normal camera distance
notes: Both named item subjects are clearly visible in full-resolution production-camera captures.

subject: named character silhouettes
defect: Many distinct named roles in Tidewake and Stormwood repeat the same face body and outfit silhouettes
notes: Distinct named roles share visual appearances; repeat appearances for the same recurring character are excluded. Tidewake has a particularly large same-outfit trainer cohort. Judged from normal-camera post frames only.

subject: uniformed character readability
defect: Dark uniformed officers and trainers blend into the purple rainy forest and lack legible rank or individual markers at normal camera distance
notes: The storm and rain read coherently; the character foreground separation is weak in these full-resolution post frames.

subject: grass around named characters
defect: Dense pale grass reaches knee to waist height around Tidewake characters and hides much of their costume silhouette in normal-camera post views
notes: The person remains visible in these frames; separate grass-at-lens and cliff-facing shots are marked as capture gaps.

subject: catch aim readability
defect: The capture chance and aim reticle sit on the target and busy grass with little separation from flowers and the throw arc
notes: The numeric chance changes are present but small; the aim view does not expose the target health as a clear visual cause. Judged from full-resolution stills.

subject: catch sequence camera framing
defect: The catch camera jumps from a wide aim view to a tight downward view that crops the companion and breaks the player-to-target spatial link
notes: The abrupt scale change and crowded impact cluster are visible across sequential production captures; no timing judgment is made from stills.

subject: catch effect finish
defect: The oversized opaque magenta ground ring and flat cream orb lose depth beside the detailed creature during the catch sequence
notes: Resting and shaking stills have little visible difference; motion and audio need separate review before judging shake timing.

subject: catch result hierarchy
defect: Catch result text competes with persistent creature cards actions and nearby same-species bodies
notes: The breakout and success wording is clear but the caught individual and inventory destination are not visually prominent in these stills.

subject: fight camera and creature scale
defect: The oversized ally often fills half the combat view and hides the trainer opponent or player while some frames clip into creature geometry
notes: South bridge r05 is nearly all clipped creature texture; a fixture position may contribute. Warden arena frames 03 05 and 08 show the encounter better. Same combat camera may recur in other biomes but is scored from Meadows evidence only.

subject: fight tell and hit effects
defect: Tells and openings rely mainly on text while flat magenta ground loops and pale radial hit rays obscure creature poses
notes: HP bars and Staggered wording do change clearly. Stills cannot establish animation timing or audio quality.

subject: Warden arena boundary
defect: Thick straight turquoise rails outline the Warden floor and cross creature silhouettes like exposed guide geometry
notes: The effect repeats through several Warden combat phases in the stronghold arena.

subject: trainer defeated presentation
defect: The bridge grunt and Warden remain upright in similar neutral postures after victory while banner and dialogue carry most of the state change
notes: The reward and Warden dialogue are readable; Warden a01 is camera-obstructed and excluded from this finding.

subject: live current streaks
defect: Live currents use long bright evenly spaced parallel white streaks that read like guide lanes on the water surface
notes: Live and restored states are visibly different at all four fixed camera stands. The live streaks supply most of the difference; still pairs do not establish flow animation timing.

subject: current restoration environment
defect: The restored current removes the white flow streaks while shoreline sandbars water color and surrounding geometry remain visually unchanged
notes: The overlay change is clear; a broader environmental transformation may depend on progression context outside these four fixed views. Confirm intended art direction before assigning scene work.

subject: named NPC post readability
defect: Several named Cloudreach NPCs look small behind the foreground trainer and show little pose or costume detail to communicate their role
notes: Post survey camera placement contributes to this framing; reshoot from conversation distance before attributing the issue to runtime interaction camera or character art.

subject: flight pose distinction
defect: The flying creature and dangling trainer keep nearly the same spread-wing silhouette in the glide and perch-approach stills
notes: The approach_perch frame remains airborne with no landing contact; capture a real landing and perch before judging the full transition. The chosen path against a dark pillar also reduces silhouette contrast.

subject: Glass Sink landmark
defect: The named Glass Sink appears as an abrupt unmarked terrain edge over a uniform checker-textured void; the sink shape and glass material do not read from reachable rim viewpoints
notes: Three camera passes from walkable rims failed to reveal a recognizable sink. The authored marker is inside nonwalkable terrain and both day and golden views show a sheer edge. Confirm intended landmark geometry and a safe authored viewpoint before assigning a fix.

subject: surface swimming trainer pose
defect: During the swim crossing the submerged trainer remains upright with relaxed arms and visible boots so the action reads as wading rather than surface swimming
notes: Code-blind review of seven unique clean frames. Dry approach and exit look grounded. Stills establish the static pose but cannot establish temporal stroke animation or movement speed.

subject: swimmer water contact
defect: The moving trainer leaves little localized wake splash foam or displaced-water ring while a hard dark shadow sits beside the body
notes: Code-blind review; strongest in entry surface_mid surface_far and surface_east. Transparent shallow water makes the lack of contact cues conspicuous.
